reason: The hypothesis relies on a mechanistic chain linking Ti content, lattice distortion, phonon softening, and enhanced electron–phonon coupling to higher Tc. The cited evidence (E1) only notes that Ti-rich Nb-Ti alloys have better superconducting properties and higher upper critical fields, without providing any data on lattice distortions, phonon spectra, or electron–phonon coupling. E2 reports robust superconductivity under pressure for a specific HEA but does not address the role of Ti content or the proposed mechanism. Thus, the core mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Lattice distortions from atomic size mismatches alter the phonon spectrum in BCC HEAs.
These lattice distortions enhance electron–phonon coupling.
Increased Ti content accentuates lattice distortions in Ti-rich BCC HEAs.
Enhanced electron–phonon coupling elevates Tc and may alter the upper critical field.
Ti-rich Nb-Ti-based alloys exhibit higher upper critical fields than Nb-Ta-based ones.
